name: TotalEnergies

points.text: Revenue is growing 41.1% year over year (strong).
Earnings jumped +123% versus a year ago, but that mostly reflects a depressed prior year.
Operating margin is 17.0%.
Return on equity is 17.8%.
Debt/equity is 46% (conservative leverage).
Free-cash-flow margin is 6.5% of revenue.
It trades at 7.4x forward earnings.
PEG ratio is 0.64 (price paid per unit of growth).
Price is 3.7% above its 200-day average: the long-term trend is up.
The 50-day average is above the 200-day average (bullish alignment).
RSI(14) is 38: sellers in control.
MACD is negative and falling: momentum is deteriorating.
It is 9.5% below its 52-week high.
22 Wall Street analysts rate it 1.8/5 on average (buy).
The average analyst price target implies 19.1% upside.
Over 6 months it returned +3.3% versus -1.7% for the MSCI World benchmark.
Last month: -6.9%.
Annualised volatility is 24%.
Worst peak-to-trough fall in the past year: 17.5%.
Beta of 0.04: defensive, moves less than the market.
No exposure to Energy yet — this would diversify the portfolio.

debate.said: Here is the case for owning TotalEnergies. Revenue is growing 41.1% year over year (strong). It trades at 7.4x forward earnings. PEG ratio is 0.64 (price paid per unit of growth).
I'm not convinced. MACD is negative and falling: momentum is deteriorating. RSI(14) is 38: sellers in control.
Price action is noise over a few weeks; the business is what we own — revenue is growing 41.1% year over year (strong). Weakness can be an entry point.

risk: Maximum position size: 19% of the portfolio (scaled for 24% volatility).
Every order costs a €1 fee, like on Trade Republic. Stop-loss rule: review at -15% from cost.
chair: Weighted committee score is +0.34 on a scale of -1 to +1; 5 of 5 analysts lean the same way. Conviction: Medium.
Decision: BUY. We propose a position of up to 19% of the portfolio.
